There is no end in sight for the drivers of illegal mining, while police action appears ineffective
Cora Bailey has been encountering illegal miners ever since she first started treating injured animals in the townships around Roodepoort, west of Johannesburg, in 1991. But as the price of gold has soared, so too has activity in the abandoned mine shafts that mark the area.
In late September, dozens of zama zamas – the name given to illegal miners in South Africa, meaning roughly “to take a chance” in Zulu – arrived to dig for gold across the dirt road from her charity, Claw (Community Led Animal Welfare).

topArticle.title: Côte d'Ivoire President: Re-globalization an opportunity to move beyond traditional trade
topArticle.description: "Re-globalization presents an opportunity for developing countries to move beyond their traditional areas of specialization in exporting primary products, and to occupy a more prominent place in the spheres of innovation, transformation, industrial production and marketing." That was the key message on 29 October of H.E. Alassane Ouattara, President of Côte d'Ivoire, who delivered the latest edition of the Presidential Lecture under the WTO’s Presidential Lecture Series.
topArticle.titleJa: コートジボワール大統領：「再グローバル化は伝統的貿易を超越する機会」
topArticle.summary: コートジボワール大統領は、再グローバル化が途上国にとって一次産品輸出からイノベーション、工業生産へと移行する機会だと述べた。
